question.lead:
Information for participants


Principal Investigator

Dr. Marcel Schreiner
Julius-Maximilians-University of Würzburg
Röntgenring 11, D-97070 Würzburg
Telefon: +49 931-3183380
E-Mail: marcel.schreiner@uni-wuerzburg.de

Study Information

Dear study participant,

Thank you for your interest in participating in our study. The goal of our research is to better understand the mental processes and behavior of humans. This research study is about how people update their beliefs when presented with new evidence. You will read descriptions of scientific studies and will be asked to rate the quality of these studies and categorize them into scientific disciplines. You will further answer questions regarding the quality of scientific studies more generally. Your reactions will be recorded through keypresses and mouse clicks, as well as response times. We will further collect data on your browsing behavior during the study (e.g., track whether the browser tab is changed during the study) and collect demographic information, such as age, gender, and education. After completing the study, you will receive more detailed information about its content and background.

This study is conducted by the work groups Cognition & Behavior of the University of Würzburg, Cognitive Psychology of the University of Mannheim, Social Cognition and Decision Sciences of the University of Tübingen, Knowledge Construction of the Knowledge Media Research Center in Tübingen, Social Psychology and Research Methods of the University of Freiburg in Germany, and the Management and Organizations Area, Fuqua School of Business at Duke University.

Participation requirements

To participate in this study, you must be at least 18 years old, speak English, and be a US resident.

Duration and Compensation

The survey will take between 20 and 30 minutes. For participating, you will receive a compensation of £3.75 via Prolific.

Voluntariness and Confidentiality of Data

Participation in the study is voluntary. You may decline to answer any question and you have the right to withdraw from participation at any time without any disadvantages. Withdrawal will not affect your relationship with the University of Würzburg or any of the other mentioned universities in any way. If you do not want to participate simply close the browser window. Even if you terminate the study prematurely, you are entitled to compensation for the time spent up to that point. Personal data (age, gender, etc.) will be recorded only to the extent necessary. The data and personal communications described above will be treated confidentially. For example, those project employees who have personal data through direct contact with you are subject to confidentiality. Your research data will be stored with a numerical code generated independently of your name. That means no one can associate your data with your name. The recorded research data will be stored, analyzed, and published (e.g., in scientific journals or internet databases) in an anonymized form.

Since your data is collected for research purposes, it will be kept for at least 10 years after data analysis or publication of the study. The results and data of this study may be published in scientific publications and made publicly accessible on the internet. This is done in an anonymized form, i.e., without the data being attributed to a specific person. This study thus follows the recommendations of the German Research Foundation (DFG) and the German Society for Psychology (DGPs) to ensure research quality. Please also note Prolific's Participant Privay Notice (https://prolific.notion.site/Participant-Privacy-Notice-6b6cb4f60a674d96a1433bff6412215b)

If you have any questions about the study contact the researcher via Prolific or contact Marcel Schreiner (marcel.schreiner@uni-wuerzburg.de) or Maren Mayer (maren.mayer@iwm-tuebingen.de) via E-Mail. If you have questions about your rights or are dissatisfied at any time with any part of this study, you can contact the researcher anonymously if you wish or email the address provided above, or contact the data protection officer of the University of Würzburg (info@uni-wuerzburg.de/datenschutz@uni-wuerzburg.de).

You are free to screenshot and/or print this information page and the declaration of consent below for your own records.

We appreciate your time and effort for this research study.

Declaration of Consent

I have been informed in writing about the study and its procedure.

I understand that personal data is collected for scientific purposes. The distribution, storage, and analysis of data relevant to this study will comply with legal requirements and require my voluntary consent before participating in the study. I consent to the data, which was collected as part of this study, being recorded and stored anonymously on questionnaires and electronical storage devices, and possibly published (e.g., in form of a scientific article). Because the data will be stored in an anonymized form, it cannot be traced back to me. I have had enough time to make a decision and am willing to participate in the described study. If I had any questions about the study, they were satisfactorily answered by the researcher. I know that participation is voluntary and I can stop participating at any time without giving a reason.

question.title: All radioactivity is man-made.
Lasers work by focusing sound waves.
Electrons are smaller than atoms.
Which gas makes up most of the Earth’s atmosphere?
Does the Earth go around the Sun or does the Sun go around the Earth?
How long does it take for the Earth to go around the Sun?
Antibiotics kill viruses as well as bacteria.

Two scientists want to know if a certain drug is effective against high blood pressure. The first scientist wants to give the drug to 1000 people with high blood pressure and see how many of them experience lower blood pressure levels. The second scientist wants to give the drug to 500 people with high blood pressure and not give the drug to another 500 people with high blood pressure, and see how many in both groups experience lower blood pressure levels. Which is the better way to test this drug?

A doctor tells a couple that their genetic makeup means that they’ve got one in four chances of having a child with an inherited illness. Does this mean that if their first child has the illness, the next three will not?
Does this mean that each of the couple’s children will have the same risk of suffering from the illness?
Imagine that we roll a fair, six-sided die 1000 times. Out of 1000 rolls, how many times do you think the die would come up as an even number?
In the BIG BUCKS LOTTERY, the chances of winning a $10.00 prize are 1%. What is your best guess about how many people would win a $10.00 prize if 1000 people each buy a single ticket from BIG BUCKS?
In the ACME PUBLISHING SWEEPSTAKES, the chance of winning a car is 1 in 1000. What percent of tickets of ACME PUBLISHING SWEEPSTAKES win a car?
Fill in the missing number.

question.title: If the chance of getting a disease is 10%, how many people would be expected to get the disease out of 1000?

Suppose you have a close friend who has a lump in her breast and must have a mammogram. Of 100 women like her, 10 of them actually have a malignant tumor and 90 of them do not. Of the 10 women who actually have a tumor, the mammogram indicates correctly that 9 of them have a tumor and indicates incorrectly that 1 of them does not have a tumor. Of the 90 women who do not have a tumor, the mammogram indicates correctly that 80 of them do not have a tumor and indicates incorrectly that 10 of them do have a tumor. The table below summarizes all of this information.

Tested positiveTested negativeTotals
Actually has tumor9110
Does not have tumor108090
Totals1981100

Imagine that your friend tests positive (as if she had a tumor), what is the likelihood that she actually has a tumor?
If it takes 5 machines 5 min to make 5 widgets, how long would it take 100 machines to make 100 widgets?
A bat and a ball cost $1.10 in total. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?

In a lake, there is a patch of lily pads. Every day, the patch doubles in size. If it takes 48 days for the patch to cover the entire lake, how long would it take for the patch to cover half of the lake?

question.title: Please read the following information carefully!
question.lead:
In the following, you will be presented with a series of 24 science news.

After the presentation of each piece of news, you are asked to rate the quality of the presented research.

When you completed the quality rating for all 24 pieces of news, you are asked about quality of research in general.

By clicking on Next you can start with the first news.

Thank you for your participation!

We would like to thank you very much for helping us.

Information about the background of the study

In this study, we investigate which types of information people use, or how much they weight certain types of information, when judging the quality of a scientific study. We also investigated the impact of longer and shorter articles. The results of this study will be used for another study, in which we want to investigate how people change their beliefs about the truth of certain hypotheses depending on the quality of the presented research. The results of the current study will be used to determine how we can influence the perceived research quality and what types of articles we should use.

For this purpose, you have been presented fictitious study results. To our knowledge, the hypotheses presented in this study have not yet been examined in scientific studies.

This means that the study results (hypothesis confirmed or rejecteed) were generated purely at random and do not allow any statement about the actual validity of the hypotheses. The names of the study authors and universities were also randomly assigned to the presented articles.

Nothing you read in this study allows to draw conclusions regarding the validity of the presented study outcomes! Unfortunately, we were not able to provide you with this information at the beginning of the study, as this may have distorted our results. We apologize for this necessary procedure.

If you have any questions, you can contact the study coordinators (Marcel Schreiner, contact: marcel.schreiner@uni-wuerzburg.de; Maren Mayer, contact: maren.mayer@iwm-tuebingen.de).

By clicking Next you will end the study and be redirected to the Panel website.
